synopsis: Minto’s Pyramid Principle is presented as an executive-communication practice and a consulting counterpart to BLUF, using a situation-complication-question-answer opening [f16446, f9851]. Chapter 12 places it alongside military BLUF, Amazon’s six-page narrative and PR/FAQ, the UK Treasury Five Case Model, and Strategic Decisions Group’s Decision Quality [f9851]. The corpus reports finding no direct controlled evidence that pyramid structures, BLUF or six-page narratives improve technical programme approval or success, so these should be treated as practitioner formats rather than proven performance interventions [f9853, f10141].

relations.note: Both identify Minto’s situation-complication-question-answer opening and connect it with BLUF.
Both report no evidence of improved approval or success and classify formats as unproven practices.
Qualifies the listed practitioner formats with the absence of direct controlled effectiveness evidence.
